findings.title: safe_urlopen for OAuth token exchange can crash view on network/transport failure
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the call `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` happens outside the try/except. The subsequent `try` only protects `safe_urlread(req).decode(...)` and `dict(parse_qsl(body))`. If GitHub's OAuth token endpoint is unreachable, times out, or otherwise raises (which safe_urlopen can do for connection/DNS/SSL errors), the view raises an unhandled exception and the user gets a 500 instead of the friendly 'Invalid installation request' page described in the PR. The PR claims the pipeline will fail gracefully when GitHub cannot generate an access_token, but a transport-level failure to the token endpoint bypasses that handling entirely. Wrap the safe_urlopen call (or its network I/O) in the same try/except so the failure mode is the documented one.

findings.title: get_user_info call can crash view on GitHub /user API failure
findings.body: `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` on line 434 is invoked with no exception handling. If GitHub's /user API call fails (network error, invalid/expired token causing 401, JSON parse error, etc.), get_user_info raises and the view returns a 500. This directly contradicts the PR description, which promises a graceful 'Invalid installation request' page when an access_token cannot be produced/used. The token-exchange try/except needs to extend (or a separate try/except needs to wrap get_user_info) so failures fall through to the existing `return error(...)` paths on lines 432/436.

findings.title: KeyError when Integration.metadata lacks 'sender' field
findings.body: The check `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` (line 504) assumes every Integration row has a `sender` dict in its metadata. That is not guaranteed: `build_integration` only adds `integration["metadata"]["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and the webhook is not guaranteed to have populated pipeline state by the time build_integration runs (or sender may be absent for integrations created via other code paths). For any subsequent install attempt where an existing Integration with status=ACTIVE happens to lack `sender`, accessing `["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the generic 'Invalid installation request' failure. Use safe access, e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`, and treat a missing sender as a mismatch (or as an explicit 'could not verify' failure).

findings.title: test_installation_not_found actually exercises the state-mismatch path, not the 404 path
findings.body: The test posts the OAuth callback with `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline signature `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` used elsewhere in this file. With the new OAuthLoginView in front of GitHubInstallation, the `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` check at line 412 fires first and returns the default `error(...)` page containing 'Invalid installation request.' The 404 stub on `/app/installations/{installation_id}` (and the `installation_id` GET that precedes it) is therefore never reached, and the assertion that replaced the original 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' check is now effectively asserting the generic-error branch. Either rename the test (e.g. test_oauth_state_mismatch) and drop the dead 404 stub + installation_id GET, or pass the matching state so the flow actually proceeds to build_integration and exercises the 404 path it claims to cover.

findings.title: Hardcoded webhook signature is brittle to INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE changes
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch posts a webhook with `HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE="sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486"`. This signature is the HMAC-SHA1 of `json.dumps(webhook_event)` (the modified INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE) under the test GitHub webhook secret. Any change to INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE content or formatting silently invalidates the signature: the webhook handler returns 401, no Integration is created with `sender="attacker"`, the subsequent OAuth/setup GET no longer hits the sender-mismatch branch, and the test fails at `assert resp.status_code == 204`. Compute the signature in-test from the body and the configured webhook secret (e.g. via hmac.new(secret, body, hashlib.sha1).hexdigest()) so the fixture and the signature stay in sync.
